thread:
cai: Heads up — nightly evals (quantized nightly run) had 14 timeouts out of 120 jobs last night. Mostly in the long-context sampler jobs.

cai: Logs show repeated `worker lost heartbeat` and the process stuck in `sleep(30)` inside our harness worker.

eva-bot: [automated] nightly-run-2026-03-19: 14 failures, rerun scheduled. Full log at https://s3.redwood/ci/nightly/2048501234/logs.tar.gz

lina: Can you paste the minimal log snippet? grep + tail is fine.

cai: sure — here's the relevant tail from one worker:

```
2026-03-19T02:11:04Z worker[pid=4521] INFO start sample loop
2026-03-19T02:11:07Z worker[pid=4521] DEBUG step 1234 took 0.012s
2026-03-19T02:11:07Z worker[pid=4521] DEBUG entering sleep for 30s (backoff)
2026-03-19T02:11:37Z watchdog ERROR missed heartbeat for worker pid=4521
2026-03-19T02:11:37Z harness ERROR killing worker pid=4521 due to heartbeat timeout
```

cai: The weird bit is the `entering sleep` is an explicit sleep in our sampling loop when we think the GPU is idle — but the GPU was active (token generation).

jasper: That suggests a scheduler/timer glitch where the process gets preempted and the explicit sleep overruns wall-clock, but the code still logs entering sleep after the generation step. Could be CPU frequency scaling or host suspend jitter. Seen that with ondemand governor and power management before.

ryan: Any OOMs or GPU faults in dmesg?

cai: dmesg is clean. GPU metrics show continuous kernel activity for that period. So the worker thought it should back off even while GPU busy.

lina: Could it be that the worker polls a condition and then calls `time.sleep(backoff)` instead of `Event.wait(backoff)` so it cannot be woken by the async callback? That would explain getting stuck for the full backoff.

jasper: Good call. I just grepped the repo — harness v0.87 has `time.sleep` in two places inside the sampling loop. We changed one to `await asyncio.sleep` in a later refactor, but not both. If the blocked code is in a thread doing synchronous GPU IO, `time.sleep` can freeze the event loop.

cai: Repro guide I ran locally: `SINGLE_WORKER=1 ./harness --profile quant-nightly --iter 2000 --seed 42` then attach `strace -p $PID -f` when it appears stuck — I see `nanosleep` showing up for 30s.

ryan: Nice repro. Can you open a small patch: replace `time.sleep` with `worker.sleep_or_yield(backoff_ms)` helper that uses `Event.wait` or `select` to be interruptible by the stopper?

lina: I'll take the patch. Also suggest adding a test that simulates a concurrent wakeup and ensures we don't block for full backoff.

jasper: For short term, bumping the watchdog threshold from 20s -> 60s will reduce noisy timeouts while we ship the fix. But we should avoid masking the root cause.

cai: Agreed. I'll open two PRs: one quick watchdog bump + metric to distinguish "blocked sleep" vs "no activity", and a second proper fix to make sleeps interruptible.

cai: PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/4321 (watchdog bump) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/4322 (interruptible sleep + unit test).

eva-bot: [ci] PR 4321 passed unit tests, queued for canary deploy.

ryan: After canary, let's run a targeted nightly with the same quantized workload and monitor failures. Also add sampling debug logs (short) around sleep calls.

lina: I'll add the unit test today and land the interruptible sleep change.

cai: Thanks — assigning follow-up to @jasper for postmortem notes and to @ryan for canary run. I'll create the incident ticket with timeline. :thumbsup:

jasper: Filing the postmortem draft now.

lina: ETA for proper fix -> EOD my timezone, will post PR link when ready.

cai: Closing loop here — will re-run the failing job set once 4322 is deployed and report back tomorrow morning. :coffee:
